Snap Soars 7% as Deutsche Bank Says Its Subscription Story Is "Better Than the Tape Suggests" ©Marcela Ruth Romero from Ruty Romero's Images and mohamed abdelghaffar from Pexels via Canva
Key Takeaways

Snap shares rose 7% after Deutsche Bank kept its Buy rating and $8 target, saying investors underrate its subscriptions.

Paid subscribers rose 77% to about 30 million last quarter, bringing in about three-quarters of Snap's added revenue.

Meta Platforms, Pinterest and Reddit all grew revenue far faster than Snap's ads, so the slowdown looks like Snap's own.

The stock looks cheap on forward earnings, though those exclude about $1 billion a year of stock pay.

Snap (SNAP:NYSE) shares are up 7% today, after Deutsche Bank's Benjamin Black argued last week's post-earnings selloff missed what's driving the business. His Nov. 10 note is titled "Better Than the Tape Suggests; Subs Mix and Earnings Power Matter."

Reddit (RDDT:NYSE) is up 7% too. But the note goes straight at Snap's weak spot: its ad business barely grew last quarter, while Meta Platforms (META:NASDAQ) and Pinterest (PINS:NYSE) kept growing at double-digit rates.

30 million people now pay for Snapchat

Paid subscribers rose 77% to about 30 million in the third quarter, and other revenue, mostly subscriptions, jumped 84% to $350 million. Advertising grew just 4% to $1.37 billion. So subscriptions brought in about three-quarters of the revenue Snap added. Black wrote: "Subscriptions increasingly matter to both the quality of revenue and the margin story, yet we think this remains underappreciated by investors."

Analysts expect revenue to keep climbing through 2028:

Snap (SNAP): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ billions, fiscal 2023-2028 (TIKR)

Black sees subscription revenue of about $1.81 billion in 2027, up about 35%, against consensus of roughly 11% growth for the whole company. Gross margin rose from 55.3% a year earlier to 62.3% in the third quarter.

Snap (SNAP): gross margin (%), last 8 quarters (to September 30, 2026) (TIKR)
Snap's ad problem is its own

North American daily users fell 6% to 92 million.

Rivals aren't seeing the same thing. Meta grew third-quarter revenue 26% to $64.6 billion. Pinterest grew 12%. And Reddit grew revenue 53% as its daily users rose 12%. Advertisers are still spending, just less with Snap, which is why subscriptions matter so much.

Cheap, with one big caveat

Black's $8 target is about 60% above Snap's close before today's jump. The stock traded at 6.6x forward earnings at the last close, well under its one-year average of about 12x. But those normalized earnings leave out roughly $1.05 billion of stock pay this year.

title: Parents Lend Daughter $50K To Clear Debt, Then Sibling Finds Signs Of About 10 New Loan Accounts Despite Her $115K Salary. ‘She Denies It’

Parents Lend Daughter $50K To Clear Debt, Then Sibling Finds Signs Of About 10 New Loan Accounts Despite Her $115K Salary. ‘She Denies It’
surprised man and wife with laptop (Credit: Photo: Nenad Cavoski/Shutterstock)

A couple lent their daughter $50,000 to pay off her debts. Years later, she was earning $115,000 a year and still hadn't paid them back. Then her sibling found records suggesting she took out about 10 new loans.

"She denies it and refuses to show statements," her sibling wrote on Reddit.

The Loan Was Supposed To Clear The Slate

The poster's sister lived with their parents and kept telling them she'd pay back the informal loan.

About three years after their parents lent her the money, the poster found approvals from several payday-style lenders. Their sister had no mortgage, yet her bank statements showed she was running short of money and getting charged fees when payments didn't go through.

She later borrowed $40,000 to buy a car, the only major purchase the poster knew about. By then, their parents were worried, and the poster was frustrated that they still couldn't tell where their sister's pay was going.

She Said She Had $20,000 Saved

The poster's sister denied having any questionable debt. She said she had $20,000 in savings but wouldn't show a bank statement.

The poster saw payments to Bitcoin trading platforms and investment companies. They also found emails about Etsy marketing and wondered if their sister was paying for a subscription.

"Every time I approach her, she shuts down, and we get into an argument," the poster wrote. Their parents found it even harder to talk to her about money.

A commenter said the family went too far by looking through her records, and the original poster agreed. They only told their sister about a few letters they saw. The more the OP found out about their sister's finances, the further apart they felt the family grew.

The poster still didn't know how much their sister owed or which loans were unsecured. Once borrowers know what they owe, Accredited Debt Relief can help them see which unsecured debts may qualify for relief.

42% Upside for Reddit? Guggenheim Thinks So, and Here's How ©Brett Jordan from Pexels via Canva and sasirin pamai's Images via Canva
Key Takeaways

Guggenheim cut its Reddit price target to $140 from $170 on Nov. 10 and kept its Buy rating.

Reddit is 62% below its January high after warning that search traffic from Google is falling and that daily users could drop in the fourth quarter.

Guggenheim's target works out to about 16x the earnings analysts expect over the next twelve months, below the stock's 25x average over the past year.

Guggenheim's $140 depends on Reddit's logged-in users continuing to grow. Reddit's fourth-quarter report in early February will show whether they are.

Reddit (RDDT:NYSE) is 62% below its January high, and Guggenheim still rates it a Buy. On Nov. 10, the firm cut its price target to $140 from $170, which is still 42% above the stock's Nov. 10 close of $98.67.

Google took the traffic

The damage came with Reddit's third-quarter report on Oct. 29. Revenue rose 53% to $895 million, but CEO Steve Huffman wrote in the shareholder letter that search referral traffic "was down meaningfully in Q3, with the decline accelerating later in the quarter."

U.S. daily active uniques fell 2% from a year earlier to 50.7 million, and Huffman warned on the call that if October's trend held, total daily users "could fall in Q4, by a low double-digit percentage" from 130 million. Fourth-quarter revenue guidance of $1.00 billion to $1.03 billion works out to 38% to 42% growth, down from 53%. The stock lost 34% in the week after the report.

Reddit (RDDT) is back in focus after the company reported third quarter earnings on October 29, 2026, along with fresh fourth quarter revenue guidance and an update on its ongoing share repurchase program.

Reddit's latest earnings and buyback update hit a stock that has been under pressure for much of 2026, with the share price climbing 1.38% on the day and 4.54% over the past week but still down 40.53% on a 30 day share price return basis and 60.68% year to date, while the 1 year total shareholder return has fallen 53.43%. This signals short term momentum around results against a backdrop of weaker longer run performance.

Scan beyond Reddit's sharp drawdown and see how other beaten up but financially solid companies compare by running the 40 high quality undervalued stocks alongside this latest earnings and buyback story.

Reddit now appears to be a business posting solid revenue and profit figures, even though the stock has been hammered this year. After that sharp drawdown and modest rebound, is the current price actually fair value for what you get?

Most Popular Narrative: 78% Undervalued

The narrative fair value for Reddit of $423.68 sits far above the latest close at $95.10, which puts the spotlight firmly on why such a wide gap exists according to John_Eric, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community who built this valuation and wrote the narrative that underpins it.

But past 60%, something flips. A discount that big is more often a sign my model is missing something than a sign the market is wrong. The market doesn't usually hand out fifty-plus percent off a genuinely good business for no reason, so before that number pulls me in, I go find the reason. If I can't find one, I assume I built the model wrong before I assume I found a once-in-a-decade gift.

Result: Fair Value of $423.68 (UNDERVALUED)

Still, the Reddit story could be knocked off course if the Google content standoff breaks against the platform or if US user engagement weakens further from here.

Find out about the key risks to this Reddit narrative.

Another View: Reddit Through The P/E Lens

There is a different read on Reddit when you look purely at earnings multiples. The stock trades on an 18.5x P/E, which is roughly double the US Interactive Media and Services sector at 9x, yet below the peer average of 37.2x and under the fair ratio of 27.1x that the market could move towards. That mix of richer pricing than the wider industry but cheaper terms than close comparables leaves a real question for investors. Is this a mispriced growth story or simply a premium that needs more proof to hold?

title: Reddit COO Says “Over 80% of Our Monetization” Is Logged In. Google Is Squeezing the Rest
detail:
Reddit COO Says “Over 80% of Our Monetization” Is Logged In. Google Is Squeezing the Rest

Reddit COO Says "Over 80% of Our Monetization" Is Logged In. Google Is Squeezing the Rest ©@Brett Jordan from Pexels via Canva; @Corina Ciocirlan's Images via Canva
Key Takeaways

Reddit stock closed at $95 on Friday, down 37% in three months and just above its 52-week low.

Third-quarter revenue rose 53% to $895 million, but CEO Steve Huffman warned daily users could fall by a low double-digit percentage.

COO Jen Wong says logged-in users drive over 80% of monetization, and those users are still growing.

At about 11x forward earnings with $3 billion of net cash, Reddit's February 5 report is the next test.

Reddit (RDDT:NYSE) closed at $95 on Friday, down 37% over three months and only about 7% above its 52-week low of $89.

The trouble comes from Alphabet (GOOGL:NASDAQ). Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode answer more questions on Google's own pages, and Reddit says that cut its search referrals by more than 1 million a week in October.

Pinterest (PINS) sold off the same day after its third-quarter revenue grew just 12% and missed its own outlook. Reddit grew more than four times as fast, yet it now trades at about 11x forward earnings.

Strong quarter, shrinking audience

The third quarter was strong:

Revenue up 53% to $895 million, above the $878 million consensus

Net income of $283 million, or $1.40 per share, up 74%

Free cash flow of $363 million, nearly double a year earlier

Revenue is up about 2.6 times in two years…

Reddit (RDDT): total revenue, quarterly, $ millions, Q3 2024–Q3 2026 (TIKR)

The warning came with the guide. Fourth-quarter revenue is guided to $1.00 billion to $1.03 billion, up 38% to 42%, and the midpoint sits below the roughly $1.05 billion consensus.

Huffman also said daily active uniques could fall by a low double-digit percentage from about 130 million if search referrals keep sliding.

The users who pay are still here

Most of the lost traffic is logged out: people who land from a Google search, read one thread and leave.

Those visitors earn Reddit very little. As COO Jen Wong put it on the call, "Over 80% of our monetization sits on the shoulders of logged-in in-app users."

So Reddit is leaning into that base. It plans to test a primarily logged-in experience in select markets outside the U.S. this quarter, and it's already testing ad placements in its search pages.

Its margins give it room to experiment. Compare them with Pinterest's:

Reddit (RDDT) vs Pinterest (PINS): EBITDA margin (%), quarterly, Q3 2024–Q3 2026 (TIKR)

Reddit's adjusted EBITDA margin hit 45% last quarter, and the guide implies about 49% for the fourth.
